equity.level_reason: Only sex and age are compared, with no social-position framing; age ≥18 defines the population.

level_alternative.reason: Group-specific results by sex and age are reported and described, though age and sex alone stay at level 0 under the brief.

ev.q: For every age group, women were more likely than men to always use sunscreen.
The percentage of men who always used sunscreen was lowest among those aged 18–29 years (8.2%)
The percentage of men who always used sunscreen was lowest among those aged 18–29 years (8.2%) and increased to 13.7% among those aged 30–44
The percentage of women who always used sunscreen was lower among those aged 18–29 and ≥65 years (25.7% and 27.7%, respectively)

notes: Age groups are compared within each sex (4 groups each); recorded as one groupwise entry. Survey weighting is not stated, so it is not recorded as a procedure. Women-vs-men contrast within every age group is read as stratified.
view_issues: Difference claims (lowest, lower, more likely) are made with CIs shown as error bars but no test or comparison method stated.
